links.outcome: Self-consistency of GPT-4o recommendations across repeated prompts versus expert order consistency
links.effect: GPT-4o exhibited high self-consistency across repeated prompts, surpassing the consistency observed among individual expert orders in the earliest round of consensus.
links.quote: We found that GPT-4o exhibited high self-consistency across repeated prompts, surpassing the consistency observed among individual expert orders in the earliest round of consensus.

links.outcome: Precision and recall of GPT-4o lab test orders versus expert consensus gold standard on simulated cases
links.effect: Precision was moderate to high (68-82 %) but recall was lower (41-51 %), indicating a risk of underutilization; prompting strategy, complexity, and setting did not significantly affect performance.
links.quote: Precision was moderate to high for both prompting strategies (68-82 %), although relatively lower recall (41-51 %) highlighted a risk of underutilization.

unlisted_practices: Chain-of-thought versus zero-shot prompting for laboratory test ordering
Alignment of LLM test recommendations with local test menus and guidelines

screen.reason: The study empirically evaluates GPT-4o on simulated clinical cases for lab test recommendations, comparing prompting strategies (zero-shot vs chain-of-thought).
